audit.evidence: Real published npm minimist bytes via aliases minimist@1.2.1(v0)/1.2.5(v1)/1.2.6(v2) invoked by minimal node:20 HTTP service (real setKey()). 4-way closure on real Docker: original@v0 flag (__proto__), blocked@v1 (string __proto__ guard), bypass@v1 flag (constructor.prototype past string guard), residual@v2 blocked (isConstructorOrProto).

app_purpose: Tiny JavaScript CLI argument parser (npm `minimist`, by substack; now maintained at github.com/minimistjs/minimist). `minimist(argv)` turns `--a.b.c value` style flags into a nested options object: it splits a dotted flag key into a path and deep-sets it via the internal `setKey(obj, keys, value)`, which walks each segment (creating intermediate namespaces) and assigns the leaf.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in minimist's setKey() deep-set. A dotted flag key is split on '.' into a path and each segment is dereferenced with `o = o[key]` (creating a namespace when absent), so a crafted segment `__proto__` (seed) makes the walk step OUT of the fresh result object and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS a property to it. The pollution is GLOBAL (it mutates the real shared Object.prototype), so the harness restores (deletes) the injected property before and after each probe. The incomplete fix (CVE-2020-7598) added a guard that names only the string '__proto__'; it is bypassed (CVE-2021-44906) by a `constructor.prototype` key chain that the guard never inspects -- the walk reaches Object.prototype through Object's `constructor`/`prototype` and pollutes it.
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL NUANCE (verified against the real npm tarballs, setKey() read at every tag, not just aggregator metadata): the setKey() STRING guard `if (key === '__proto__') return;` was introduced by CVE-2020-7598's 1.2.3 release; minimist@1.2.3/1.2.4/1.2.5 carry the byte-identical '__proto__'-only guard; minimist@1.2.6 (CVE-2021-44906 fix) replaces it with `isConstructorOrProto(o, key)` (= `key === 'constructor' && typeof o[key] === 'function' || key === '__proto__'`). V1 is pinned to 1.2.5 -- the last release before 1.2.6 -- so the V1->V2 step is the exact CVE-2021-44906 incomplete-fix boundary. V0 is pinned to minimist@1.2.1, the last release whose setKey() has NO __proto__ handling at all (grep '__proto__' = 0 hits), so the plain `--__proto__.pcbUnlock` seed genuinely pollutes on V0 and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real differential on the same sink). NOTE: minimist@1.2.2 was re-pinned AWAY from as V0 because 1.2.2 already added a PARTIAL reference-equality check `if (o[key] === {}.__proto__) o[key] = {}` that blocks the plain `--__proto__.x` seed (empirically confirmed: seed blocked on 1.2.2), so 1.2.2 is not a clean pre-guard V0. The plain-string seed represents the CVE-2020-7598-class pollution (a `__proto__` flag segment reaching Object.prototype through setKey); it is a faithful reconstruction from the advisory + source diff, not a byte-for-byte replay of a public offensive PoC. The residual argv `--constructor.prototype.pcbUnlock.x` places `pcbUnlock` one level deep so that 'prototype' is an INTERMEDIATE segment (the last-key `if (o === Object.prototype) o = {}` guard does not fire) and the intermediate reference-reassignment `o['prototype'] = {}` silently no-ops (Object.prototype is a non-writable property of Object), so the walk stays on Object.prototype and pollutes it = CVE-2021-44906.

sink: minimist index.js -- the setKey() key-loop guard on flag key-path segments. The walk dereferences each segment with `o = o[key]`; a `__proto__` segment (seed) or a `constructor.prototype` chain (residual) makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype.
residual: The '__proto__'-only string guard (V1 = minimist@1.2.5) returns from setKey only when `key === '__proto__'`; it never inspects 'constructor'. A flag whose key is a constructor.prototype chain -- `--constructor.prototype.pcbUnlock.x` (splits to ['constructor','prototype','pcbUnlock','x']) -- walks the result object to its `constructor` (the Object function), then `constructor.prototype` (= Object.prototype; the reference-reassignment `o['prototype']={}` silently no-ops on the non-writable Object.prototype), and with 'prototype' as an INTERMEDIATE segment (so the last-key `o===Object.prototype` reassignment does not fire) writes `pcbUnlock` onto Object.prototype = CVE-2021-44906. The `--__proto__.pcbUnlock` seed is blocked on V1; the constructor.prototype residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2021-44906 (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h): minimist before 1.2.6 is vulnerable to prototype pollution via the setKey() function. Snyk/Debian: the original fix for CVE-2020-7598 was incomplete as it was still possible to bypass it (the guard checked only the '__proto__' key name and not the constructor/prototype path); the 1.2.6 patch guards constructor and __proto__ via isConstructorOrProto().

provenance.notes: node:20-slim faithful-core; REAL published minimist bytes per version via npm aliases (1.2.1/1.2.5/1.2.6); the harness drives the REAL minimist() parser. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the setKey() key guard: V1 (minimist@1.2.5) guards only the STRING key name '__proto__' (`if (key === '__proto__') return;`); the residual `--constructor.prototype.pcbUnlock.x` reaches Object.prototype because the guard never inspects 'constructor' and the reference-reassignment on the non-writable Object.prototype silently no-ops while 'prototype' stays an intermediate; V2 (minimist@1.2.6) adds `isConstructorOrProto` and blocks it. V0 (minimist@1.2.1) has NO setKey() proto guard so the plain-string `--__proto__.pcbUnlock` seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. Benign canary: prototype pollution BY ADDITION flips a default-deny gate (Object.prototype.pcbUnlock absent => denied) releasing a planted PCB_FLAG; benign own-property writes never trip it. Pollution is GLOBAL (real Object.prototype), restored before/after each probe to keep probes isolated (verified: seed@v1 returns 'denied' even after seed@v0 polluted -- no cross-probe leakage). See source_verified_caveat: V0 re-pinned from 1.2.2 to 1.2.1 because 1.2.2 already carries a partial `{}.__proto__` reference check that blocks the plain seed. Gate passed on real Docker 2026-07-14.
